terms.gloss: a throw; the range of a throw
evidence: Liv. 8.7.1: vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset
terms.comment: Within range is intrā tēlī jactum; a spear’s throw away, tēlī jactū.

evidence: Liv. 28.14.19: nōndum ad tēlī conjectum vēnissent
terms.comment: ad tēlī conjectum venīre, to come within range.

terms.gloss: sight, the range of the eyes
evidence: Phaedr. App. 28.10: sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit
terms.comment: in cōnspectū, within sight; ē cōnspectū, out of sight.

phrases.latin: jamque intrā jactum tēlī prōgressus uterque substiterat
phrases.english: and now each side had come within range and halted

phrases.latin: ita ut vix tēlī jactū ab statiōne proximā abesset
phrases.english: so that he was hardly a spear’s throw from the nearest outpost

phrases.latin: vēnātor citus nōn intellēxit sēque ē cōnspectū abstulit
phrases.english: the hunter, in a hurry, did not understand, and went off out of sight

sources: Lewis & Short: jactus · Lewis & Short: conjectus · Lewis & Short: conspectus
Vergil, Aeneid 11, and Livy 8 and 28 checked against the Perseus Latin texts (9 November 2026).
